Cross City, Horseshoe Point, Suwannee, Horseshoe Beach, Shamrock,
Shired Island, Cross City Airport, Old Town, Guaranto Springs,
Eugene, Fletcher, Yellow Jacket, and Fanning Springs.

events.summary:
At 1039 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 7 miles southwest of St. Mary to near Alliance to 6
miles north of Buckhorn, moving southeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated. This storm has a history of producing tree
and powerline damage in Farmington.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile
homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

These severe storms will be near...
Perryville, Patton, and Alliance around 1045 PM CDT.
Daisy and Millersville around 1055 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by these severe thunderstorms include Old
Appleton, Glenallen, Silver Lake, Lithium, Longtown, Sedgewickville,
and Oak Ridge.

This includes Interstate 55 between Mile Markers 110 and 139.

events.region: Zapata; Jim Hogg; Brooks; Starr; Southern Hidalgo; Inland Willacy; Inland Cameron; Northern Hidalgo
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The combination of hot temperatures and humidity will produce heat
index values between 105 and 111 degrees for several hours
Saturday afternoon into Saturday evening. A few locations may
briefly experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

If spending time outside today, drink plenty of water, wear light
weight and light colored clothing, and take frequent breaks from
the heat. Young children and pets should never be left unattended
in vehicles.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southern Crawford County in east central Missouri...
Southern Washington County in east central Missouri...

* WHEN...Until midnight CDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

had ended, but areas of minor flooding will continue as the water
drains into creeks and rivers.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Potosi, Steelville, Irondale, Mineral Point, Courtois,
Cherryville, Caledonia, Davisville, Shirley, Dillard, Latty,
Belgrade, Cook Station and Cadet.

drainage and low-lying areas.

Sullivan, Cuba, Bourbon, Anthonies Mill, Leasburg, Richwoods, Old
Mines, St. Cloud and Oak Hill.

This includes the following State Parks...
Washington State Park and Onondaga Cave State Park.

This includes Interstate 44 in Missouri between exits 203 and 218.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, breaking waves of 3 to 6
feet with frequent, dangerous rip currents, highest across
south to southwest facing beaches exposed to southerly swells.
Very strong rip currents are occuring along some beaches. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected at
the times of highest tide.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Malibu Coast and
Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 AM PDT
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of sea water is likely around the time of
high tide, over low-lying coastal areas such as parking lots,
beaches, and walkways. Significant damage to roads or
structures is NOT expected. There is an increased risk of
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 5.8 to 6.5 feet will occur
in the evening hours tonight.

events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, frequent, moderate to
strong rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated surf.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 AM PDT
Saturday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of sea water is likely, around the time of
high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as
parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Significant damage to
roads or structures is NOT expected. There is an increased
risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and
surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 5.5 to near 6.0 feet will
occur in the evening hours tonight.

frequent rip currents are likely along some beaches,
especially exposed south to southwest facing beaches along the
Central Coast.

Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Southwestern
Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast and Lake
Casitas.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is an increased risk of ocean
drowning due to hazardous rip currents. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.
